newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SES lists new rules to up corporate responsibility.
newsitem.headline: SES lists new rules to up corporate responsibility.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) on Tuesday introduced new rules, effective January 1, 1997 to raise the standard of corporate governance in listed companies.
"The review has become necessary in light of recent events unveiled at Amcol which resulted largely from the failure of the company's self monitoring mechanism," SES said in a statement.

Property and trading group Amcol Holdings was placed under interim judicial management in July after a Price Waterhouse report said the company had serious cashflow problems and difficulties in meeting its financial obligations.

In the new rules, the appointment and roles of the audit committee have been enhanced to improve transparency and the standard of accountability and corporate governance in listed companies, thereby safeguarding shareholder, the statement said.

It said under the new provisions, the chief executive officer of a company cannot be a member of the audit committee. The committee should have at least three members, the majority of whom should be independent.
Directors who has vested interest in or engages in financial transactions with the listed company will not be qualified to be an independent member, SES said in the statement.
The audit committee will have an enhanced role including commissioning and reviewing findings of internal investigations into suspected frauds or irregularities, it said.
The new rules also require a listed company to appoint the same accounting firm to audit its accounts and those of its Singapore subsidiaries and associates.
SES said this is to ensure an accurate and comprehensive view of the entire group's affairs.

It cited in Amcol's case, substantial assets amounting to 73 percent of the company's total investment in principle subsidiaries and associated companies were audited by a number of different accounting firms.
SES said the new rules will take effect from the financial year beginning on or after January 1 1997.
